item.title: Hirosaki Castle & Cherry Blossoms: Japan's Best Hanami — Guide
item.description: Hirosaki Castle in western Aomori holds one of only twelve original Edo-period keeps left in Japan — but it is most famous as the country’s greatest cherry blossom site. In late April some 2,600 trees erupt in bloom, and fallen petals blanket the moat into the legendary pink ‘hanaikada’ flower raft. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hirosaki, Aomori Hours Park always open; keep ~9:00–17:00 Admission Park free; castle areas ~¥320 Time needed 1.

item.title: Sagae Cherry Blossom Festival: Hanami in Cherry Country — Guide
item.description: Sagae City’s Ohkura Dam park and the surrounding cherry orchards erupt in pink in late April — the festival combines classic hanami (flower viewing) under the blossoms with cherry-themed food stalls, local sake and evening illuminations that transform the trees into glowing pink canopies. As Japan’s premier cherry prefecture, this is one of the country’s most authentic fruit-blossom celebrations. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Sagae, Yamagata Hours Late April (peak bloom) Admission Free Time needed 1.

item.title: Mt. Yoshino Cherry Blossoms: Complete Guide — Nara
item.description: Mount Yoshino (Yoshinoyama) is Japan’s most famous cherry-blossom destination, with some 30,000 trees blanketing the mountainside in four zones that bloom in succession. A UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape, it turns pink for roughly two weeks each April and is unforgettable at dawn. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yoshino, Nara Pref. Hours Open mountain; shops daytime Admission Free (ropeway ~¥450 one-way) Time needed Half to full day Best time Early–mid April (blossoms) The Four Blossom Zones Shimo Senbon (lower) — first to bloom, near the ropeway and Kimpusen-ji temple.

item.title: Osaka Cherry Blossom Guide: Best Hanami Spots & Timing
item.description: For about two weeks each spring, Osaka turns pink. Cherry blossom (sakura) season transforms the castle moats, riverbanks, and parks into clouds of blossom, and the city throws itself into hanami — flower-viewing picnics under the trees, by day and (lit up) by night. From the iconic combination of blossoms and Osaka Castle to the riverside tunnels of the Kema Sakuranomiya and the once-a-year Japan Mint passage, Osaka has some of the Kansai region’s best and liveliest cherry-blossom spots.

item.title: Tokyo Cherry Blossom Guide: Best Hanami Spots, Timing & Etiquette
item.description: There is no week in the Japanese calendar more celebrated than sakura season. For about ten days each spring, Tokyo — a city of 14 million people — pivots its entire social life around sitting under trees. Friends, families, and colleagues converge on parks from early morning to claim prime spots, spread blue tarps, and spend the afternoon eating, drinking, and staring upward at a canopy of pale pink that will be completely gone in a week.

item.title: Chiba Events & Festivals Calendar: From Narita Setsubun to Kujukuri Fireworks
item.description: Chiba’s event calendar spreads remarkably evenly across the year — there are compelling reasons to visit in every season. The prefecture’s Pacific coast produces its most distinctive spectacles in winter (flower fields, whale watching, the Setsubun bean-throwing at Naritasan) and spring (the Isumi Railway rapeseed season, Katsuura’s hina doll festival), while summer brings fireworks over Tokyo Bay and Pacific beach culture. This guide covers the major events worth planning a visit around.
